transcription.prompt: A child aged 10 to 15 in India answers a teacher aloud in Hindi, English, or a Hindi-English mix. Write Hindi words in Devanagari and English words in Latin script, exactly as spoken.

move.shape: they asked for it another way: a new, simpler way in — not the words you used before; open with one concrete everyday situation — kit contexts: exam marks, cricket match wins, plant growth; ask what they think will happen or which they would pick — a prediction, no right answer yet; any bigger/more comparison: two quantities of one kind, in one unit — a count against a count, a distance against a distance; never across kinds; mention once: at the end they will teach this to Bittu (a pretend new student who missed this class); address them with aap forms only (aap, aapka, aapne; verbs -iye / -enge), never tum or tu
move.must: a different example or question from the last one, never the same one again
